transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-10-02
Start: 11:00 AM PT
Duration: ~50 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Adagio Head of Platform), Ethan Wu (Adagio SRE), Samira Khan (Adagio Product)
Recording: yes (auto)

Summary: quick tour of Redwood Console route-level telemetry, per-route cost breakdown, and a plan to run a short pilot with Adagio production traces. Quick security touchpoints on VPC/KMS and SOC 2 were requested.

Topics: console route dashboard, cost attribution, batching & quantization recommendations, pilot logistics, security & compliance notes.

Action items (captured above) and next steps summarized at the end.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intros — I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and Diego is our solutions engineer. We'll walk through a route-level telemetry snapshot from the Console and then look at how that maps to cost.
[00:18] Priya Rao: Hi maya, thanks. We're curious specifically about splitting cost per model route — we have about 120 routes in front of our API gateway and want to stop overpaying on background tasks.
[00:35] Diego Alvarez: Great. Today I'll share my screen and show a few artifacts: the Route Usage Lens, per-route token breakdown, and a cost attribution table that ties tokens + model variant to dollar units.
[00:50] Ethan Wu: Quick note, our stack is mostly k8s on GCP, some internal inference endpoints, and we want VPC or private deployment options for compliance.
[01:08] Maya Chen: Absolutely — we'll cover hosted vs dedicated vs private options and typical latency/cost tradeoffs.
[01:22] [Screen share starts]
[01:30] Diego Alvarez: Ok showing Console home -> Insights -> Route Usage Lens. At the top you can filter by timewindow, model, and deployment type. This is a snapshot from a customer with similar QPS to Adagio. There's a map of routes ranked by token volume.
[01:52] Samira Khan: Looks nice. Can you show a per-route breakdown that includes average latency and cost per 1k tokens?
[02:05] Diego Alvarez: Yep. Clicking the route shows a panel: tokens, median p50/p95 latency, cost-per-token, and recommended optimizations — for example batching, prefix caching, or switching to a quantized variant. Note: some of the model names here get truncated in the UI — the transcript OCR sometimes shows "redwood opti-mizer" instead of Redwood Optimize.
[02:35] Priya Rao: Is the cost-per-token a static estimate or based on recent usage? We need near-realtime mapping to billing to justify team-level chargebacks.
[02:50] Diego Alvarez: It's computed from recent usage windows (by default 24h) and backfilled to monthly views. You can pin a specific pricing profile — e.g., hosted m-standard vs dedicated with reserved capacity — and the Console will recalc the cost projection.
[03:12] Ethan Wu: How do you deal with prefix/KV cache accounting? A lot of our prep prompts are shared across routes.
[03:25] Diego Alvarez: We surface prefix cache hits as a separate column — you'll see reduced token counts attributed to the route and the Console suggests caching coverage. The "kayv cache" phrase in older transcriptions is a common mis-hear — it's KV cache.
[03:45] Maya Chen: To illustrate impact: in the sample dataset route A had 40% of its tokens served from KV cache, lowering per-call cost by about 28%.
[03:58] Priya Rao: Nice. Can we set per-route alert thresholds? We want to know when cost per route spikes beyond a baseline.
[04:12] Diego Alvarez: Yes — Alerts -> New -> Route anomaly. You can track cost/tokens/latency. We also integrate alerts into Slack and your incident system via webhooks.
[04:28] Samira Khan: What about deduping between similar routes? We sometimes have many near-duplicates for A/B tests.
[04:40] Diego Alvarez: There's a route grouping feature where you can create logical groups and run aggregate cost attribution across them. We also export group-level CSVs for finance teams.
[04:58] [timestamp jump]
[05:20] Diego Alvarez: Now opening the Cost Attribution table — it breaks down spend by model variant, tokens, and route, and shows a hypothetical reserved-capacity savings projection. You can toggle quantization recommendations — e.g., int8 vs fp16 — and see delta to latency.
[05:45] Ethan Wu: Are model variants auto-picked for fallbacks? We have strict p95 latency SLOs for some routes.
[05:57] Diego Alvarez: Yes, the Smart Routing policies can prefer low-latency variants for certain routes and fall back to cheaper variants when load is degraded. That can be configured per-route.
[06:14] Priya Rao: Security — SSO + RBAC is must-have. Also need audit logs and KMS support for keys.
[06:28] Maya Chen: Redwood supports SAML SSO, per-team RBAC with role templates, and audit logs with configurable retention. For Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM. We'll include SOC 2 docs in the follow-up.
[06:45] Priya Rao: Do you have documented network architecture for Private (VPC) deployments? We need diagrams for security review.
[06:56] Maya Chen: Yes — we'll attach an architecture diagram and a VPC connectivity checklist.
[07:10] [timestamp jump]
[07:30] Diego Alvarez: Switching to Optimize recommendations — this view looks at token distribution and suggests batching window sizes and cache lifetimes. For example, increasing micro-batch from 8 to 16 reduced per-token CPU by 12% in a similar workload.
[07:55] Samira Khan: Any guardrails on batching vs latency? Some of our routes are user-facing chat.
[08:06] Diego Alvarez: You can set route-level max-latency SLOs and Optimize will only recommend batching for routes that have headroom. The Console simulates expected p95 impact when suggesting batch sizes.
[08:26] Priya Rao: If we want to pilot: what's the easiest path?
[08:34] Maya Chen: Typical path is: 1) we ingest a representative sample of traffic (sample traces), 2) Redwood runs a replay in a sandbox to produce a heatmap, 3) we run a short pilot on hosted or dedicated capacity with traffic replay. Diego will run a microbenchmark first so you can see delta numbers.
[08:54] Ethan Wu: Replay — is there an agent or do we upload traces?
[09:02] Diego Alvarez: Both options. You can upload gzipped trace files or use our lightweight replay tool that runs from your environment. We'll provide a template.
[09:15] Samira Khan: I want to see the actual dollar difference if we move 30% of background routes to quantized models.
[09:24] Diego Alvarez: We'll produce a per-route delta projection in the follow-up CSV. The Console also has a "what-if" simulator where you can toggle quantization and reserved capacity.
[09:40] [timestamp jump]
[10:00] Priya Rao: On compliance, do you support data residency? Some customers require EU-only data for certain routes.
[10:10] Maya Chen: Yes — region routing can pin routes to specific regions or private deployments. For EU-only routes we'd recommend Private or Dedicated in EU regions.
[10:25] Ethan Wu: For dedicated, how long are contract minimums and is bursting allowed?
[10:32] Maya Chen: Typical reserved capacity terms are monthly or annual with burst buffers. We'll include the committed terms in the pricing sheet; Diego will call out typical throughput per GPU unit during the microbench.
[10:47] Samira Khan: Any examples of customers using per-route chargeback for finance?
[10:53] Maya Chen: Yes — several customers export the per-route CSV and import into their internal chargeback tools. One customer used Redwood Console to identify 15 routes that were background tasks and moved them to cached workflows, saving 23% on gross spend.
[11:10] [timestamp jump]
[11:30] Diego Alvarez: I'll show the CSV export: includes columns route_id, route_name, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_hits, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, cost_estimated_usd. It's commonly imported into BigQuery or Snowflake.
[11:55] Priya Rao: If we wanted to turn that into daily automated reports to finance, is there an API?
[12:02] Diego Alvarez: Yes — the Console exposes a Reporting API and webhooks. We can also set up a scheduled export to your storage bucket.
[12:20] Samira Khan: Any pitfalls with token counting across different model families? We use a mix of GPT-style and open-llama variants.
[12:31] Diego Alvarez: We normalize token counting at the tokenizer layer and attach a model-family tag so you can map tokens to model-specific costs. There are edge-cases but we surface notes in the CSV for any mismatched tokenizer heuristics.
[12:50] Priya Rao: Ok this is helpful. Could we get a sample export for our most expensive day last month?
[12:57] Maya Chen: Yes — Priya if you can share a list of the top-10 routes and a CSV of sample traces, Diego will run local replay and we'll return a cost heatmap and the sample export.
[13:15] [timestamp jump]
[13:30] Ethan Wu: One more: do you instrument internal fallbacks? We want to understand when requests are automatically rerouted to cheaper variants and items in logs.
[13:42] Diego Alvarez: Smart routing events are logged and visible in the trace view. There's a toggled column for fallback_reason and fallback_variant.
[13:55] Samira Khan: Great. We'll want to see an annotated example.
[14:00] Maya Chen: We'll attach an annotated example in the follow-up.
[14:07] [wrap-up section]
[14:15] Maya Chen: Quick recap: Diego will run the microbench and replay with Adagio samples once Priya shares traces; I'll send pricing + SOC 2 + architecture diagram; we'll schedule a 60-min pilot kickoff next week pending Priya's availability.
[14:32] Priya Rao: That sounds good. Can we tentatively do pilot kickoff on 2028-10-10?
[14:39] Maya Chen: I'll propose that in the calendar invite.
[14:45] Ethan Wu: Thanks, all.
[14:48] Samira Khan: Thanks.
[14:50] Diego Alvarez: Thanks everyone — talk soon.

End of transcript. Notes: some auto-transcription oddities remain (model names truncated, occasional "kayv" instead of KV, and Speaker attribution swapped once). Follow-up artifacts to be uploaded to CRM: pricing sheet, SOC2, VPC diagram, and microbenchmark results.
